name: Brixton
description: Deep terracotta bleeding into ember-red — the heat and pressure of a neighbourhood that has always had too much expected of it

name: Stockwell
description: Amber-red, warm but not quite settled — a border district between south London's gravity and the pull of Zone 1

name: Vauxhall
description: Amber-gold in flux — MI6 glass and Pleasure Gardens, old vice and new money sharing the same riverside air

name: Pimlico
description: Amber shading toward gold — stucco terraces and quiet money, close enough to Westminster to feel its gravity

name: Victoria
description: Cool white-gold, the colour of departure — five million suitcases a year and the coaches lined up for everywhere else

name: Green Park
description: Pure cool white-gold, near-white — the most expensive earth in England lies directly above this station

name: Oxford Circus
description: Cool white-gold with a retail shimmer — the most footfall of any tube station outside Waterloo, a city of strangers in constant orbit

name: Warren Street
description: Neutral amber — a commuter station that asks no questions, quietly adjacent to the NHS and the teaching hospitals

name: Euston
description: Industrial orange — the gateway for the north, half-demolished and half-rebuilt, perpetually on the edge of becoming something else

name: King's Cross St. Pancras
description: Industrial orange — twenty years of regeneration visible in one glance, the coal yard turned into flats, the canal turned into a destination

name: Highbury & Islington
description: Warm amber in a postcode that gentrified faster than anyone expected — the Arsenal crest still on the walls, the fans mostly gone north

name: Finsbury Park
description: Warm amber-red — the park, the megastore mosque, the Eritrean restaurants, the bike-hire racks; a junction of many Londons

name: Seven Sisters
description: Amber-red, murky at the edges — the market under the railway arch and the names of the dead on the war memorial, unhurried by money

name: Tottenham Hale
description: Warm amber-red thinning toward brown — the retail park and the bus interchange, the Lee Valley beyond, somewhere to be from

name: Blackhorse Road
description: Warm amber — the breweries and the studios and the Walthamstow Wetlands beginning just out of frame, still becoming

name: Walthamstow Central
description: Clean amber, slightly melancholy — the end of the line, William Morris's birthplace, the longest street market in Europe closing its stalls at dusk
